budget.rationale: The six reconciled categories total $5,700–$8,900, comfortably below both the $12,000 target and $15,000 preferred maximum. Exact June 2027 airfare and lodging are not quoted, so the favorable score is medium-confidence.

weather.rationale: IPMA's Funchal June normal is mild and relatively dry, while official Madeira guidance warns that mountain conditions can differ and trails can close. Flexible day order manages, but does not remove, cloud and wind.

swim.rationale: The plan includes managed Lido and Porto Moniz entries plus Machico, but June Atlantic water is refreshing rather than warm and every swim remains conditional on flags and swell.

variety.rationale: Within one island the itinerary schedules a city, gardens, volcanic pools, a mist forest, high peaks, a dedicated PR6 25 Fontes/Risco levada day, an exposed headland and two low-output reset days.

ease.rationale: The family sleeps in the same apartment all week, skips ferries and extra flights, enjoys two car-free days and reaches the airport in about 20–30 minutes. The transatlantic connection is the only reason this is not a 5.

food.rationale: The Funchal base has apartment cooking and current supermarket coverage, while every named road stop includes pizza, grilled chicken, fries or a packed-lunch fallback. Exact 2027 menus and hours remain unconfirmed.

risk.rationale: The one-base plan avoids compounding logistics, but Madeira Airport wind, unpublished exact June 2027 protected routing, trail closures and Atlantic swell remain material managed risks.

nights.rationale: Seven hotel nights keep this intentionally short and easy to fit into the year. In a comparison that gives more length points to vacations of nine nights or more, this earns 1/5.

novelty.rationale: The family has not visited Madeira before, so both the island and this scenery-first style of trip feel genuinely new.

pto.rationale: Using the observed Juneteenth holiday keeps the trip to only five vacation days, the strongest time-off fit in the comparison.
